findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Say that the `.git`-scoped retry handler is passed as `onexc=` on Python 3.12+ and through `onerror=` (adapting the exc_info triple) on 3.11, so the cleanup works on every version allowed by `requires-python`.

findings.finding: The plan calls `shutil.rmtree(basetemp, onexc=...)` with no version guard. `onexc` was added in Python 3.12, but the project supports Python 3.11 and up, so on 3.11 the test would fail with `TypeError: rmtree() got an unexpected keyword argument 'onexc'` before any cleanup runs.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the rmtree cleanup uses `onexc` on Python 3.12+ and `onerror` (taking the exception from `exc_info[1]`) on 3.11, because requires-python is >=3.11.
evidence: Plan: "In `test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py`, `shutil.rmtree(basetemp, onexc=...)` clears the bit and retries only for paths inside a `.git` directory"
pyproject.toml:16 `requires-python = ">=3.11"`; .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:420 `python-version: ["3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]` and test.yml:336 `uv venv --python 3.11`
Python docs (shutil.rmtree): 'Changed in version 3.12: Added the onexc parameter, deprecated onerror.'
tests/unit/test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py:94-97 already has `if sys.version_info >= (3, 12): ... onexc=... else: ... onerror=lambda f, p, ei: ...(f, p, ei[1])`
findings.finding: The plan says the cleanup test uses `shutil.rmtree(basetemp, onexc=...)` but does not mention a fallback for Python 3.11. The onexc keyword only exists from Python 3.12, while the project declares requires-python >=3.11 and CI runs 3.11 jobs. Taken literally, the call raises TypeError on 3.11. The existing test file already branches to onerror on 3.11, but the plan does not keep or require that branch.
scenarios: The Linux 3.11 matrix job or the minimum-dependency 3.11 job runs test_completed_snapshot_test_leaves_basetemp_removable and fails with TypeError: rmtree() got an unexpected keyword argument 'onexc'.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the bullet to say: `shutil.rmtree(basetemp, onexc=h)` on Python ≥3.12, else `shutil.rmtree(basetemp, onerror=lambda f, p, ei: h(f, p, ei[1]))`, where `h` clears the read-only bit and retries only for paths inside `.git` and re-raises everything else. This matches the branch already at test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py:94-97.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the old alert_store lock target is used anywhere else, and justify (or mitigate) mixed-version appenders after switching to the sibling '.append.lock'.
evidence: 'alert_store.append serializes through rebar._store.fsutil.sibling_exclusive_lock(today, lock_name=".append.lock")'
The plan has no mention of mixed-version or other lockers of the alert file.
findings.finding: Moving alert_store.append from an fcntl lock (src/rebar/reconciler/alert_store.py:14-17,51-59) to a sibling '.append.lock' changes the lock identity on POSIX too, not only on Windows. The plan does not address mixed-version writers, where an old process locks the old target and a new process locks the sibling, nor any other code that locks the alert file directly.
scenarios: During an upgrade, an old and a new reconciler append concurrently on POSIX. They take different locks and interleave writes.
